FOLLOW-UP ANALYSIS · SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 · ORIGINAL SCORES PRESERVED

Separate missing information,
source limitations, and reviewer behavior

Historical cohort: September 2026. These reports describe frozen generic-v7/v8 records and their September 12 CBORG reference rescore, not the current generator or a current validation of its outputs. Saved render metadata dates v7 to September 1–2 and v8 to September 5 (VOICE replicate 1) or September 7 (the other 11 records). Labels beginning 2026-09-04f/g are run identifiers, not the generation dates of all v8 records. Provenance recording timestamps are distinct from exact model-call start times; see the saved VOICE v8 replicate 1 and CM4AI v8 replicate 2 records.

CM4AI generation-regime caveat. V8 replicates 2 and 3 returned no thinking block in the full, reconciliation, report, and report re-check phases. The historical requests omitted the thinking parameter; the generation analysis documents an input-correlated adaptive outcome, not an explicit request to disable thinking or an established proxy fault. Both replicate 2 and replicate 3 remain included in every original score and pooled result. The pooled CM4AI comparison therefore mixes observed thinking regimes. This limits attribution of differences to the v8 package alone; it does not establish that the regime explains any score difference or justify a corrected score.

The follow-up adds 10 figures, structural-presence checks, review-overlap measures, uniform item-removal sensitivity analyses, and an evidence assessment of 32 stratified comments. The main change is interpretive: reviewer labels are useful signals, but they are not a direct census of missing fields or verified factual errors.

Evidence-review boundary. The 32-comment assessment is an assistant review of frozen D4Ds and selected historical source excerpts. It is neither a human-validated gold standard nor an estimate of error prevalence in all 562 comments. Compound comments can contain both supported and overstated claims. No original D4D, evaluation score, or evaluator text was changed.

Original report and exploratory tests · Implementation plan · Complete downloadable bundle

What changes—and what remains stable

  • The earlier missing-field figure was a review-conditioned view. All 24 records omit top-level download_url, imputation_protocols, parent_datasets, and resources; only 18, 13, 12, and 9 records respectively receive completeness comments naming those fields. Structural absence is not automatically an error or an applicable requirement.
  • Stable scores conceal substantial variation in commentary. Repeated rubric10 scores differ by only 0–2 percentage points, while mean pairwise overlap of flagged fields is 54–73%. Requiring the review family to match lowers overlap to 28–47%.
  • Version directions survive the disputed-item sensitivity. With Q19 omitted uniformly, AI_READI remains slightly lower in v8, CHORUS higher, and CM4AI and VOICE lower. Removing Q13 as well does not change those directions. These are diagnostic score subsets, not corrected scores or stronger causal evidence.
  • Several sampled allegations need reinterpretation. The DOI-format inconsistency in S30 is contradicted by the historical schema; S12 overlooks an explicit software/data license distinction; S22 compares local version numbers across separate deposits; S24 treats the source’s V2/2.0 display conventions as a defect.
  • Some supported concerns remain actionable. Release-specific temporal coverage, processing-software provenance, component repository identifiers, and demographic detail remain incomplete in selected D4Ds. S32 exposes adult/pediatric scope ambiguity in generated wording. The review does not establish that all these gaps were fillable from the supplied sources.

Completeness has several meanings

The selected 16 fields produce 384 record–field pairs. Of 242 structural absences, 144 are named by at least one completeness comment and 98 are not. These counts describe reviewer attention to selected structural gaps; they do not estimate recall because applicability and source-supported expected content were not established.

Important correction to a tempting interpretation: download_url is defined in the historical schema as a URL pointing directly to the data, distinct from a landing page. Its absence should not automatically be “fixed” by inserting FAIRhub or Dataverse access pages. In S19, the access route is already structured under distribution_formats.access_urls.

Evidence examples distinguish several levels: S01/S19 have an access route elsewhere; S25 contains a selective variable summary plus referenced dictionaries; S05’s source explicitly says no DPIA was conducted but the dedicated D4D field is empty; S31 records the same kind of negative declaration in a populated field. These should not all receive the same completeness interpretation.

Low cross-rubric overlap is not automatically poor reliability: the instruments ask different questions. Repeat-review overlap is more directly relevant to evaluator stability, but covers only four fixed records and still spans documented execution changes.

Strict signature grouping reduces 562 comment entries to 538 record-specific signatures; the broader definition yields 536. This small reduction shows that exact field-set matching is too conservative to serve as a complete semantic deduplication. The selected-topic figure is a readable complement, not a claim that we have counted distinct errors.

The original exploratory tests and their multiple-comparison adjustments remain unchanged; no new significance claim is made.

Item distributions and ceiling effects

Per-record diagnostic scores · Version contrasts · Item counts

Evidence review of 32 comments

Sampling used seed 20260930 and selected one primary comment per dataset × rubric × review family. Correctness and content_accuracy form one family. Within each stratum selection was uniform from issue IDs sorted lexically. The result is balanced over those strata, not over severity or population frequency. This sample contains no high-severity comments; it cannot characterize the most severe issues. The sampling probabilities and stratum sizes are retained.

Primary dispositionSample commentsInterpretation
Representation / selective summary6Content exists elsewhere, coverage is selective, or the concern is classification/readability. Not necessarily an inaccurate result.
Documented source differences8Source wording, dates, units, or roles differ; the D4D often preserves the distinction.
Explicit source limitation2The source explicitly says an assessment was not done; documentation fidelity and underlying practice are separate.
Documentation gap; provenance unresolved6A D4D gap is supported, but whether the source corpus allowed it to be filled remains unsettled.
Reviewer claim overstated or contradicted5At least one allegation conflicts with the record/schema or overinterprets a source convention; mixed components remain.
Inherited wording or citation convention3The questionable string or format comes from the source or its recommended citation.
Generated scope ambiguity2The generated wording insufficiently separates release scope from project or companion-dataset context.

Concrete corrections and proposed clarifications

  • Analysis framing: replace any shorthand “18 missing download URLs” with “18 records had a completeness comment naming an absent download_url; the field is structurally absent in all 24.”
  • Evaluator claim, S30: bare doi plus CURIE id conforms to the historical schema; split off the separate publisher-field concern.
  • Evaluator claim, S12: the record explicitly distinguishes the software MIT license from the data’s access agreement. Preserve the narrower missing-license-detail concern.
  • Evaluator claims, S22/S24: distinguish separate Dataverse deposits and the source’s own V2/2.0 display conventions.
  • D4D wording, S32: describe four adult disease categories plus controls in the adult-release paragraph; identify pediatric data as a separate companion release.
  • D4D wording, S20: mark the three-condition AP-MS description as preprint/project context, then state the current release’s treated-condition scope.

These are proposed interpretation and wording corrections. No source D4D or original score was edited. The case table below preserves the original comment, evidence, proposed action, and uncertainty.

32 cases

S01 · AI_READI_v8_rep1 · rubric10

Representation / selective summary

Original label: completeness; severity: low. Issue AI_READI_v8_rep1_r10_rating1:3. Stratum size: 26.

No download_url field is populated. The download route is nevertheless reconstructable from page, data_governance.access_review_process (verified-ID login, T2DM-only attestation, license assent) and the external resource https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, so the sub-element's purpose is met by platform access instructions rather than by a direct link.

Assessment: download_url is unpopulated, but the FAIRhub access route and conditions are stated in data_governance and external_resources. The historical schema distinguishes a direct data URL from a landing/access page, so this is not proof that download_url should contain that page.

Action: Retain access instructions; populate download_url only if a source supplies an appropriate direct retrieval URL.

Uncertainty: No direct-download endpoint was established; no live access test.

S02 · AI_READI_v8_rep2 · rubric10

Documented source differences

Original label: consistency; severity: low. Issue AI_READI_v8_rep2_r10_rating1:3. Stratum size: 16.

The de-identification evidence carries an internal tension the record itself surfaces: is_deidentified.deidentification_details reports the FAIRhub deIdentType as 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentHIPAA true, while is_deidentified.method asserts the public set is stripped of PHI 'via the Safe Harbor method'. The record reconciles this by explaining that no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification step was necessary, which is a coherent reading, but the two statements read as contradictory in isolation.

Assessment: The D4D preserves two source statements: FAIRhub says no identifiers were collected and no active de-identification was necessary; the Nature comment says the public set is stripped using Safe Harbor. The comment itself accepts a coherent interpretation.

Action: Attribute each statement to its source and release scope rather than treating either as established false.

Uncertainty: The actual processing history is not resolved by these documents.

Record and source evidence

S03 · AI_READI_v7_rep3 · rubric10

Documented source differences

Original label: content_accuracy; severity: medium. Issue AI_READI_v7_rep3_r10_rating1:2. Stratum size: 9.

is_deidentified.method simultaneously reports that the FAIRhub dataset description records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' and that the public set is stripped of PHI 'using the Safe Harbor method', with identifiers_removed listing HIPAA PHI plus sex, race/ethnicity and medications. The two statements describe the same release and pull in opposite directions; the record flags the tension but leaves the structured method value carrying both readings.

Assessment: Both quoted de-identification statements are present in the D4D and recoverable from separate source chunks. This is a source tension carried into the record, not evidence of an invented statement.

Action: Separate source-specific statements and distinguish collection from public-release filtering.

Uncertainty: Historical-publication and current-metadata scope may differ; no operational adjudication.

Record and source evidence

S04 · AI_READI_v8_rep3 · rubric10

Documented source differences

Original label: semantic_understanding; severity: low. Issue AI_READI_v8_rep3_r10_rating1:9. Stratum size: 6.

Unresolved institutional attribution: the acronym expansion ('Exploratory' versus 'Equitable'), the lead institution (Washington University in St. Louis as FAIRhub managing organization and license Licensor versus University of Washington as RO-Crate PI affiliation and NIH RePORTER awardee) and the publisher (FAIRhub versus AI-READI Consortium) each differ between equally ranked sources. The record carries both positions in source_caveats rather than asserting one silently, which is the correct handling, but a consumer of creators.principal_investigator.affiliation receives two affiliations for one person.

Assessment: The record explicitly reports conflicting institutions and publisher values. Source excerpts name Washington University in St. Louis in the license/FAIRhub metadata and University of Washington in RO-Crate investigator affiliation.

Action: Preserve role-specific attribution and the source caveat. Seek steward clarification before choosing a single institution.

Uncertainty: Different organizational roles can coexist; the sources alone do not prove which attribution is wrong.

Record and source evidence

S05 · AI_READI_v7_rep3 · rubric20

Explicit source limitation

Original label: completeness; severity: medium. Issue AI_READI_v7_rep3_r20_rating1:3. Stratum size: 14.

data_protection_impacts is not populated even though the record documents processing of protected health information under HIPAA Safe Harbor, a controlled-access tier holding zip code, genetic sequencing data and medication history, and an explicit residual re-identification risk. The substance of an impact analysis is present (participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, future_use_impacts risk-and-mitigation statements, Level 3 data security classification), but no formal DPIA slot or document is referenced.

Assessment: The field is absent, and the historical FAIRhub healthsheet explicitly says a data protection impact analysis has not been conducted. The assessment artifact is a source-level absence; the negative statement itself could have been captured.

Action: Populate an explicit negative finding with its source, without inventing a DPIA or interpreting scattered privacy discussion as a formal assessment.

Uncertainty: No conclusion about whether a formal assessment is legally required.

Record and source evidence

S06 · AI_READI_v8_rep2 · rubric20

Documented source differences

Original label: consistency; severity: medium. Issue AI_READI_v8_rep2_r20_rating1:1. Stratum size: 30.

is_deidentified is internally contradictory. method states 'No active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected' and simultaneously that 'The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the Safe Harbor method'. deidentification_details then records the FAIRhub value deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification' alongside deIdentHIPAA true and deIdentDirect true. 'No de-identification was necessary', 'Safe Harbor stripping was performed' and 'NoDeIdentification' cannot all describe the same processing step; identifiers_removed further lists four categories actively removed (PHI, sex, race/ethnicity, medications), which is an active removal, not an absence of need.

Assessment: The same tension noted in S02 appears in two sources and is reproduced in the same record. The reviewer gives it a stronger interpretation here, but those documents do not determine whether collection and release filtering describe one processing step.

Action: Make the source and processing-stage distinction explicit.

Uncertainty: A same-step contradiction cannot be established from the available excerpts.

Record and source evidence

S07 · AI_READI_v8_rep3 · rubric20

Documented source differences

Original label: content_accuracy; severity: medium. Issue AI_READI_v8_rep3_r20_rating1:5. Stratum size: 18.

Institutional attribution is internally divided: Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) is recorded as accountable organization, managing organization and Licensor, while the IRB (STUDY00016228), the Human Subjects Division, the assay laboratory (UW Nutrition and Obesity Research Center) and the custom environmental sensor lab (Karalis Johnson Retina Center) are all University of Washington. The ROR identifier does match the name it is attached to, so this is a source conflict rather than a malformed identifier, but the governance chain as asserted places accountability at an institution that performs none of the documented oversight functions.

Assessment: The record names differing institutions and discloses the provenance of each. The review infers that accountability cannot lie with an institution not listed for operational oversight; that inference is not established by the source excerpts.

Action: Keep organizational role and source attached to each attribution.

Uncertainty: The accountable organization cannot be independently settled here.

Record and source evidence

S08 · AI_READI_v8_rep2 · rubric20

Representation / selective summary

Original label: semantic_understanding; severity: low. Issue AI_READI_v8_rep2_r20_rating1:11. Stratum size: 5.

Device heterogeneity is not categorized as a bias. Retinal imaging was acquired on four OCT/OCTA vendor platforms (Heidelberg Spectralis, Topcon Maestro2, Topcon Triton, Zeiss Cirrus) and four fundus platforms, and the record notes that Optomed Aurora image quality 'varies from patient to patient and within the same patient'. Cross-device systematic difference is a textbook measurement_bias for multimodal imaging AI, but it appears only under anomalies, so known_biases omits a bias type that the dataset's own acquisition design makes likely.

Assessment: Device heterogeneity and image-quality variation are documented outside known_biases; known_biases lacks a measurement-bias entry. Adding that taxonomy entry is an interpretive categorization improvement, not proof a source fact was omitted.

Action: Consider a qualified measurement-bias entry that cites the documented device/site heterogeneity and labels the risk as an interpretation.

Uncertainty: The inference from heterogeneous devices to systematic bias is not empirically tested.

Record and source evidence

S09 · CHORUS_v7_rep1 · rubric10

Documentation gap; provenance unresolved

Original label: completeness; severity: medium. Issue CHORUS_v7_rep1_r10_rating1:12. Stratum size: 26.

Temporal coverage of the clinical data is unstated. collection_timeframes gives the NIH award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and its own source_caveats notes these 'are the NIH project period for award OT2OD032701, not the clinical period the admissions are drawn from'. Temporal ordering of collection, processing and publication therefore cannot be checked.

Assessment: collection_timeframes supplies grant dates and explicitly says these are not admission dates. The source excerpt confirms the grant period. The clinical temporal-coverage gap is real in the D4D.

Action: Record clinical coverage as not established in the reviewed sources and request release-specific dates.

Uncertainty: A targeted source review does not prove no relevant dates exist anywhere in the corpus.

Record and source evidence

S10 · CHORUS_v7_rep1 · rubric10

Documented source differences

Original label: consistency; severity: low. Issue CHORUS_v7_rep1_r10_rating1:11. Stratum size: 30.

Two sources disagree on scale and the disagreement is carried into the scored values: tier-2 documentation gives 50,000 admissions and 7,642 admissions with radiology data, while the tier-4 August 2025 webinar gives 'over 45K unique admissions' and 1000 images. The record discloses the conflict and unit mismatch rather than concealing it, which is good practice, but the headline counts remain contested.

Assessment: The website and webinar contain the reported numbers, and the record preserves the August 2025 qualifier and images-versus-admissions distinction. Different dates and units do not by themselves establish conflicting facts.

Action: Present numbers in a source/date/unit table; avoid treating all numerical differences as contradictions.

Uncertainty: Comparable release snapshots are not available to adjudicate an error.

Record and source evidence

D4D SHA-256: e5c0f47198cd20ea47158959f6cfb4d25648965eb8c063ac977e2b5b9aba355d. Full evidence JSON. Source snippets come from recovered historical chunks; searches were targeted, not exhaustive.

{
  "description": "The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of acute and critical care hospital admissions, assembled retrospectively by the CHoRUS Network, one of four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program. Data are contributed by 14 data acquisition hospitals among the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, whose membership is given as more than 60 consortium members. Structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit; imaging is drawn from hospital PACS in DICOM; telemetry waveforms from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware are released in WFDB; and EEG waveforms from hospital EEG databases are released in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Social determinants of health and contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are also acquired. The project website reports a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU settings, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data, against an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. The nine documented data types are demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging, waveform telemetry, and EEG waveform; every one of them is under controlled access. OMOP and telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave, clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites with only tokens centralized, and as of August 2025 imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were still in process. The project also sequesters a holdout test set for external validation of models.",

The tier-2 project documentation (chorus4ai.org) states a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions and 7,642 admissions with radiology data; the tier-4 cohort_2_webinar states that \"As of August 2025, covers 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions\" and that 1000 images are currently available. The tier-2 values are stated in this record, with the webinar's August 2025 snapshot reported where it describes modality readiness; the conflict is also recorded on the individual values it affects. The two imaging figures are expressed in different units (images versus admissions with radiology data) and may not be directly comparable. A single OTHER term in conforms_to_standard stands for three distinct standards the registered enum does not cover: EDF+, Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema. The WFDB entry likewise covers a schema the source describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset, and does not state the language of the dataset content."

S11 · CHORUS_v8_rep3 · rubric10

Documented source differences

Original label: content_accuracy; severity: medium. Issue CHORUS_v8_rep3_r10_rating1:6. Stratum size: 20.

Two volume disagreements are retained rather than reconciled: the project website reports 50,000 released admissions while the September 2025 webinar reports over 45,000 unique admissions as of August 2025; and the website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data while the webinar reports roughly 1,000 images available with de-identification in process. The record discloses both disagreements and its ranking rule, which is good provenance practice, but a reuser cannot determine the volume of the release they would receive.

Assessment: The source numbers and their qualifiers are preserved. The D4D explicitly says the imaging counts use different units. The reviewer correctly identifies unresolved release-volume specificity, but not a demonstrated inaccurate number.

Action: Use a source/date/unit comparison and distinguish snapshot coverage from current-release counts.

Uncertainty: No current release audit was performed.

Record and source evidence

Reviewer claim overstated or contradicted

Original label: semantic_understanding; severity: medium. Issue CHORUS_v8_rep1_r10_rating1:8. Stratum size: 9.

license_and_use_terms conflates two distinct objects: the MIT License applies to the chorus-ai code, while no license is named for the data. The access terms recorded are those of one route (the AIM-AHEAD training program registration), not a general data use agreement, so reuse permissions for the dataset itself remain unstated.

Assessment: license_and_use_terms.source_caveats explicitly says the MIT statement concerns software, not data, and identifies the training-program access route. This contradicts the allegation that the D4D conflates software and data licensing. Missing named data-license details remain a separate valid concern.

Action: Withdraw or qualify the conflation allegation while retaining the narrower documentation gap.

Uncertainty: This is a mixed comment; it is not wholly invalid.

Documentation gap; provenance unresolved

Original label: completeness; severity: medium. Issue CHORUS_v8_rep2_r20_rating1:9. Stratum size: 17.

prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent for a controlled-access dataset of critically ill patients' PHI. intended_uses is developed in detail across three categories, so the use guidance is one-sided: no prohibition on re-identification attempts, redistribution, or clinical deployment of unvalidated models is recorded, even though such terms are presumably in the signed licensing agreement.

Assessment: Both prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are absent. The source excerpt requires a signed agreement but does not supply its restrictions. The comment’s suggestion that specific prohibitions are presumably in that agreement is speculation.

Action: Mark the unprovided agreement terms as unknown; do not invent prohibitions based on expected practice.

Uncertainty: The unavailable agreement was not obtained or adjudicated.

Record and source evidence

S14 · CHORUS_v8_rep2 · rubric20

Representation / selective summary

Original label: consistency; severity: medium. Issue CHORUS_v8_rep2_r20_rating1:4. Stratum size: 37.

The dataset is protected health information from 14 US hospitals and confidential_elements asserts that every data type is under controlled access, but regulatory_restrictions is absent in full: no hipaa_compliant status, no confidentiality_level classification, no other_compliance. The restrictiveness asserted in prose is never expressed as a governance classification.

Assessment: Controlled access is explicitly documented, while regulatory_restrictions is unpopulated. This is a structural classification gap, not an internal contradiction. HIPAA compliance cannot be inferred simply from controlled access.

Action: Preserve the access restriction; fill a regulatory classification only when supported by a source or clearly labeled mapping.

Uncertainty: No compliance determination is made.

Reviewer claim overstated or contradicted

Original label: semantic_understanding; severity: low. Issue CHORUS_v8_rep3_r20_rating1:16. Stratum size: 7.

labeling_strategies, splits and parts of tasks describe project intentions in the future tense ('a visualization and annotation environment will label data', 'will also provision a holdout test set') and are recorded in fields whose semantics imply realized dataset properties. The record flags this at labeling_strategies.source_caveats, splits.source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats, so the intent/state distinction is preserved - but a consumer reading splits alone would infer a holdout set exists when its size, composition and availability are unstated.

Assessment: splits.split_details itself says the award abstract states the dataset will provision a holdout set, and source_caveats calls this an intention. A reader of splits is therefore not being told unambiguously that a realized holdout exists.

Action: Retain the future-tense qualifier; consider a dedicated status field if the schema permits it.

Uncertainty: Tasks may still benefit from clearer temporal scope; this does not invalidate the entire comment.

Record and source evidence

S22 · CM4AI_v8_rep2 · rubric20

Reviewer claim overstated or contradicted

Original label: consistency; severity: medium. Issue CM4AI_v8_rep2_r20_rating1:1. Stratum size: 26.

Version numbering regresses across releases: this June 2026 release declares version: '2.0', while version_access records the earlier October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) and June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) as 'version 2.1'. A successor release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors is not explained anywhere in the record, and source_caveats does not flag it among the source conflicts it does disclose.

Assessment: The compared version strings belong to different DOI-identified Dataverse deposits, each of which has its own version. Source excerpts confirm Version 2.0 for June 2026 and Version 2.1 for earlier deposits. Lower local deposit versions do not demonstrate chronological regression across datasets.

Action: Revise the reviewer’s regression claim; add a per-deposit version clarification if desired.

Uncertainty: This is a source/deposit interpretation, not a replacement score.

Inherited wording or citation convention

Original label: correctness; severity: low. Issue CM4AI_v7_rep3_r20_rating1:10. Stratum size: 14.

The keyword 'mass spectroscopy' is a terminological error for mass spectrometry, the technique actually used throughout (SEC-MS, AP-MS). Spectroscopy and spectrometry are distinct methods, so the keyword misdescribes the assay and will not match controlled-vocabulary searches.

Assessment: The keyword mass spectroscopy is present in the D4D and verbatim in the current Dataverse release metadata; the preprint also uses the phrase. It is inherited source terminology rather than evidence of a generator-created substitution.

Action: For controlled-vocabulary indexing, propose normalization to mass spectrometry with source attribution retained.

Uncertainty: The review does not quantify any actual search failure.

Original label: completeness; severity: low. Issue VOICE_v8_rep1_r10_rating1:10. Stratum size: 26.

variables enumerates only four fields (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release whose phenotype directory holds dozens of diagnosis and questionnaire tables. Column-level semantics are delegated to the per-file JSON data dictionaries, which are described but not enumerated in the record.

Assessment: variables has four entries, while file_collections describes more feature arrays and external JSON dictionaries. The D4D is a selective schema summary, not a full variable dictionary. The limited coverage is real but does not mean all variable semantics are absent.

Action: Link or inventory the relevant dictionaries and state the scope of variables; extract additional named variables only where supported.

Uncertainty: Column-level completeness cannot be scored without an expected-variable inventory for this release.

S26 · VOICE_v8_rep2 · rubric10

Documented source differences

Original label: consistency; severity: medium. Issue VOICE_v8_rep2_r10_rating1:1. Stratum size: 16.

updates.frequency states a semi-annual (twice yearly) cadence, but the release history the record itself supplies is denser and irregular: 2025-01-17 (1.1), 2025-04-16 (2.0.0), 2025-08-18 (2.0.1), 2025-12-16 (3.0.0), 2026-05-01 (3.1.0) — five releases in roughly sixteen months. The record caveats that the cadence statement was written against Health Data Nexus hosting, but does not reconcile it with the observed PhysioNet release pattern.

Assessment: The cadence statement comes from older Health Data Nexus documentation and is caveated as such. PhysioNet history mixes major releases and patches. The statements differ in platform/time scope and planned cadence versus observed events.

Action: Move the older cadence to historical context and distinguish planned major-release cadence from patch releases.

Uncertainty: Irregular realized releases do not alone falsify a stated plan.

Record and source evidence

S27 · VOICE_v7_rep1 · rubric10

Inherited wording or citation convention

Original label: correctness; severity: low. Issue VOICE_v7_rep1_r10_rating1:7. Stratum size: 12.

The RRID carried in the citation, RRID:SCR_007345, is well formed and resolves to PhysioNet, the hosting repository, rather than to the dataset itself. Using a repository RRID inside a dataset citation is a category slip: it identifies where the data sit, not the resource being cited.

Assessment: The recovered official recommended citation includes RRID:SCR_007345 alongside PhysioNet and the dataset DOI, matching the D4D citation convention. This establishes inheritance, not a generator-created identifier error.

Action: Preserve the recommended citation and, if useful, explicitly label the repository identifier separately from the dataset DOI.

Uncertainty: The RRID registry was not independently resolved during this local review.

Record and source evidence

Representation / selective summary

Original label: semantic_understanding; severity: low. Issue VOICE_v8_rep3_r10_rating1:8. Stratum size: 7.

Ontology references are given as bare CURIEs without labels or resolvable prefixes: instances carry data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69. A reader cannot determine what topic or substrate is meant from the datasheet alone, even though the same concepts are described richly in prose elsewhere in the record.

Assessment: The record contains bare B2AI CURIEs without local explanatory labels. This supports a standalone-readability concern, but the reviewer’s claim that prefixes are not resolvable was not tested.

Action: Add labels and an explicit prefix map for standalone exports if the schema/export format supports them.

Uncertainty: No ontology-resolution or correctness check of the selected ontology terms was performed.

Record and source evidence

S29 · VOICE_v8_rep1 · rubric20

Documentation gap; provenance unresolved

Original label: completeness; severity: medium. Issue VOICE_v8_rep1_r20_rating1:6. Stratum size: 23.

Subpopulations are identified categorically (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, five disease cohorts) but never quantified. No per-cohort counts, no demographic distribution, and no enumerated per-diagnosis inclusion/exclusion criteria are given, although sampling_strategies states such criteria were applied and subpopulations states the distribution is skewed.

Assessment: Subpopulation categories and imbalance are described without counts; criteria are referred to rather than fully enumerated. The source bundle has protocol inclusion criteria, but these are project/time-scoped and do not establish current-release cohort counts.

Action: Separate missing release-specific distributions from protocol detail that could be summarized with date/scope attribution.

Uncertainty: No expected demographic table or complete release-specific criteria list was reconstructed.

Record and source evidence

S30 · VOICE_v7_rep1 · rubric20

Reviewer claim overstated or contradicted

Original label: consistency; severity: low. Issue VOICE_v7_rep1_r20_rating1:12. Stratum size: 22.

Identifier rendering is inconsistent: doi is the bare string '10.13026/8xbn-nq66' while id and version_access.latest_version_doi and related_datasets.target_dataset use the 'doi:' CURIE prefix. There is no top-level publisher field, although PhysioNet is identified as host in citation, maintainers and data_governance.stewardship_roles.

Assessment: The historical schema expressly requires a bare DOI in doi and allows a CURIE in id. Thus the mixed rendering is expected, not an identifier inconsistency. The same comment also identifies a genuinely absent publisher field, whose information appears elsewhere.

Action: Remove the DOI-format allegation; retain publisher as a separate representation/completeness observation.

Uncertainty: Compound comment with one contradicted and one supported component.

Record and source evidence

S31 · VOICE_v7_rep2 · rubric20

Explicit source limitation

Original label: content_accuracy; severity: medium. Issue VOICE_v7_rep2_r20_rating1:2. Stratum size: 14.

data_protection_impacts states plainly that 'No analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted', while the same record documents biometric voice data, psychiatric and cognitive-impairment cohorts, an explicit statement that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved, and an acknowledgement that voice can never be fully de-identified. The absence of a formal DPIA is honestly disclosed and partly offset by ethicist review of sensitive fields and the published memorandum 'Ethical Justification for Controlled Access to Raw Voice Data Samples', but the substantive gap remains for a dataset of this sensitivity.

Assessment: data_protection_impacts explicitly records that no analysis was conducted; the historical source gives the same negative response. A populated negative declaration is not an inaccurate result merely because the underlying dataset has privacy risks.

Action: Keep the negative declaration and distinguish evaluation of documentation fidelity from evaluation of the dataset’s governance practices.

Uncertainty: No legal requirement or adequacy determination is made.

Record and source evidence

S32 · VOICE_v7_rep1 · rubric20

Generated scope ambiguity

Original label: semantic_understanding; severity: low. Issue VOICE_v7_rep1_r20_rating1:4. Stratum size: 8.

The description enumerates five disease cohort categories including 'pediatric voice and speech disorders', but the record's scope is the adult dataset: human_subject_research.special_populations and related_datasets state that pediatric participants were released as a separate Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset. subpopulations repeats the five-category list and then notes 'the adult dataset contains adult participants only'. A reader skimming the description could infer pediatric data is included in this release.

Assessment: The adult-release description says participants were recruited from five categories including pediatric disorders, and collection_mechanisms includes a pediatric process. Other fields correctly identify pediatric data as a separate release. This is a supported scope-clarity problem in generated wording.

Action: Revise the adult-release description to four adult disease categories plus controls; describe pediatric categories only as a separate consortium dataset.

Uncertainty: The underlying adult/pediatric dataset separation is explicit in sources; no records were inspected.

Each participant completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks recorded on a tablet application, self-reported demographic and medical history questionnaires, disease-specific validated questionnaires, and clinician-performed gold standard diagnostic validation. Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants across five North American sites. Source-type relationships: heterogeneity and linkage precision

Of 2,394 candidate source-to-comment links sharing a populated root, 1,231 involve comments naming only the root. Only 418 also have an identical normalized nested path in a receipt. This is a linkage-specificity diagnostic, not an error-source attribution rate. Array indices are removed, so even the “same nested path” category can refer to different list entries. A future claim-level analysis would need exact entry identities and entailment review.

Source-section comparisons and denominators · Candidate links · Path-match summary

Methods, validation, and presentation guidance

All 56 input references were rechecked against the stored SHA-256 hashes, covering 24 distinct D4Ds. The 48 primary ratings remain the basis of cross-rubric and version summaries; eight extra rubric10 ratings are used only for repeat agreement. Score-subset arithmetic was checked against the original totals. Historical evidence bundles were recovered using the pipeline’s run_chunks helper, which verifies the generation-time bundle/chunk identity. Historical schema descriptions were read from the registered instrument commit rather than inferred from current main.

Evidence assessments are intentionally narrow: source differences do not prove a generated falsehood; structural absence does not prove applicability; a source’s explicit “no” is meaningful content; and reviewer disagreement does not establish which judgment is correct. No internet lookups, new evaluator model calls, legal/compliance determinations, or changes to the source repository were made.

Suggested main presentation: use structural absence (15), review agreement (16), the disposition matrix (22), and version sensitivity (17) as the four new main figures. Use recurring topics (23) and source heterogeneity (21) for the narrative, with the remaining figures in supplementary material.

Suggested claim: “Structural completeness and semantic review findings measured different aspects of documentation. Repeated evaluation produced stable aggregate scores but less stable field-level findings. Several sampled correctness/consistency comments reflected source limitations, source conventions, or reviewer overinterpretation rather than demonstrated generated inaccuracies. Dataset-specific version directions persisted under uniform removal of disputed provenance items, without resolving the study’s execution and adjudication limitations.”
